headline: Citigroup chief executive Jane Fraser said AI spending is not slowing despite higher interest rates, because there is not enough computing capacity.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: said on the earnings call of Tuesday 13 October, before the window.
importance_line: A large bank lender sees no pullback in AI spending, which matters to AI companies and to the power and chip suppliers that depend on it, but it is one bank's view and the same call warned that sustained higher rates could pressure weaker borrowers.
summary: Benzinga reports that Jane Fraser, chief executive of the bank Citigroup, said on its third-quarter earnings call on Tuesday 13 October "We're not seeing a slowdown in investment in the broader AI ecosystem" and "There's simply not enough compute," with energy shortages a bottleneck. She also said AI is helping the bank cut costs: about 14,000 engineers use the Devin coding tool, and new products launch 30% to 40% faster.
notes: Benzinga page blocked (Cloudflare); text read on TradingView, which carries Benzinga's report. url is Benzinga's original.
